summary: The run wrote resolution.md with an ownership map and rewrites for all four tune-* pages (titles ≤60, metas ≤155) and named the sitemap fallback, but it never obtained the live current titles, H1s or descriptions, so no real 'before' text is shown.
met: Ownership map (one query, one owner) with conflicts is settled before the Rewrites section
One distinct query theme per page, grounded in each page's function (validator, pre-push mod, fix-then-polish workflow, release workflow)
Rewritten titles are all ≤60 chars (46, 50, 42, 48) and metas ≤155 chars (150-153); H1s are distinct across the four pages
Names the sitemap/pre-GSC fallback and invents no search data (no clicks/impressions claimed; recommends GSC re-check)
missed: Did not use the live current title/H1/meta as the 'before' for any page; the file says current tags are unknown. Ground truth shows titles were available: e.g. /tune-skill-mod/ was 'Tune Skill Mod — Claude Code mod' with H1 'Tune Skill Mod', /tune-and-ship/ had H1 'Tune And Ship'. The Bash curl was apparently denied and the run did not retry another way.

The only 'current' value cited (/tune-skill/ 'Audit and Fine-Tune…' as likely H1) is actually the title; the real H1 was 'The skill is already written. The work left is making it fire. Tune what already exists.' The run guessed and flagged it as unverified.

Meta descriptions were never compared to current ones, so the claim that these pages 'fight for the same searches' is not demonstrated from live data; the real titles show they were already fairly distinct (no duplicate titles).
Alt B/C options lack character counts for several titles/metas, and Alt B metas were not length-checked (the Alt B tune-skill meta likely exceeds 150).
skill_defects: The skill relies on a shell curl to read the live <head>, with no fallback when Bash is denied, leaving the 'before' column empty; it should instruct a WebFetch prompt that explicitly asks for the raw title, H1 and meta description, or a sitemap-fallback path that still captures them.
The skill does not require a before/after table, so a run can write rewrites without any verified current text and still look complete.
No instruction to length-check every alternate, not just the recommended option.
